messages.subject: testing user-defined functions
parts:
I am using a variety of user-defined functions in my Stan models and I don't quite trust my ability to write bug-free code... so I've taken to copying functions to R and modifying the syntax so that I can test the functions independent of the model.  It would be nice to just use Rcpp and some wrapping code to turn the Stan functions from the .cpp file (after parsing, pre-compilation) into functions callable from R.  That would make ti possible to run/test them from R.  My question is:

1) Has anyone done it?  I I have not been able to find any examples.
2) Are there any known barriers to doing this?  I have also not seen any discussion of this.

I'm interested in doing the wrapping so I'm just trying to save myself some time and grief by checking first.

Thanks!

Krzysztof

object <- stan_model(file)

you can use get_cppcode() on that or look for the .cpp file in tempdir().

Ben

There are different arguments threaded through different
types of functions. See the chapter on user-defined functions
in the manual.

The output stream is where any print() statement will be
rendered.

Any function ending in _rng gets a random-number generator
and is only usable in the generated quantities block.

And any function ending in _log can be used as a log
density using the sampling statement (~) notation with the
first argument on the left.

Any function ending in lp__ has access to the log probability
accumulator and may only be used in the model block.

There's still the issue of whether we want to relax this last
restriction to allow use in the transformed parameters block,
where we (still) allow lp__ --- it was just an oversight on my
part when implementing increment_log_prob() not to include
transformed parameters.

To see better what's going on, look at how the functions
in the following program get compiled:

return x;
}

return x;
}

return x;
}

}

  Rcpp::XPtr<boost::ecuyer1988> ptr(base_rng__);

I think I missed this when you originally posted---the file get_rng.cpp works as is on its own, it does not need to be in the same .cpp file as the Stan functions, it does not need to be in the Rcpp namespace (in fact I think that's why your attempt is not working), and it can be compiled 100% separately from the Stan function.

Krzysztof
